label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:

Replying to: none

Spent a couple Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy's shed. Not saying who or where, and none of it was his doing anyway. I kept a list of what we found. Pics below.

How the shed was getting power: three orange extension cords plugged into each other, out the basement window, across the yard and under the deck. One spot was spliced and wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. Duct tape, the silver stuff.

It gets better.

The breaker feeding all this was a 30 amp. The wire on it was 14 gauge, which is good for 15. So that breaker was gonna sit there happy as a clam while the wire cooked.

The outlet in the shed was hooked up with speaker wire. Like off a stereo.

There was a GFCI out there. I know because it had a sticker on it that said GFCI. It was a regular outlet. Somebody peeled the sticker off something and stuck it on. 26 years doing this and that's a new one. I almost respect it.

Ceiling fan was on a box held up by one drywall screw. One. Spinning over people's heads.

Mouse nest in the junction box. Mice were fine. Did not care about me at all.

Then I open the panel in the basement, and on the inside of the door in Sharpie it says SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON. My buddy's wife is standing right there and she goes "who's Ron?" Like I'd know. Like we all know each other.

I never met Ron and I'm not gonna bash him. I don't think he was a bad guy. I think he was cheap and a little proud, and that's most of these. Nobody sets out to build a firetrap. They want a light in the shed, they don't want to pay for it, it comes on when they flip the switch, so in their head it's done right. The man signed his work.

Now the not funny part. That shed worked. Probably for years. That's what gets people. This stuff works fine right up until the night it doesn't, and you don't get a warning. Cords laying under a deck in the wet, mice living in the box, a breaker that won't trip. That's everything you need. This is how houses burn down, and it's usually while everybody's asleep.

What's out there now: trench 18 inches down, 12/2 UF cable that's made to be buried, 20 amp GFCI breaker, real box, real outlets, and the fan's on a brace that'll hold it. I got paid two pizzas and a case of Yuengling. That's the buddy rate and no, it's not open to the public.

So if you need electric done, call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy who watched a video. I got nothing against YouTube, but the guy in the video has never seen your panel and he's not the one sleeping in your house. Yeah, a real electrician costs more. It costs a lot less than a new house.

And if you ever open your panel and somebody signed it, call one of us.
